title: Zoom in: buying a label when the reply is lost
caption: A timeout tells you nothing about whether the carrier bought the label. Ask by your own reference before buying again.

messages.label: label: pending, ref=shp_ab12
messages.note: Record the intent first, with a reference derived from the shipment, so a crash or timeout leaves a row to resume from.

messages.label: POST /labels ref=shp_ab12
messages.note: The reference travels with the purchase; the carrier stores it on the label.

messages.label: 201 label + tracking no.
messages.note: The carrier bought the label, but the reply is dropped on the way back. Fulfilment only sees a timeout.

messages.label: GET /labels?ref=shp_ab12
messages.note: Outcome unknown, so don't buy again blind: look the reference up.

messages.label: found: label + tracking no.
messages.note: The first purchase went through.

messages.label: label: done + outbox row
messages.note: Store the label and a label-created outbox row in one transaction. One label, one event.

scenarios.name: Blind retry
scenarios.summary: Retrying the purchase without a lookup buys a second label for the same parcel. Nobody notices until the reconciler reads the invoice.

messages.label: POST /labels
messages.note: No reference, no lookup.

messages.label: 201 label A
messages.note: Label A is bought; the reply is lost.

messages.label: POST /labels (retry)
messages.note: To the carrier this is a new purchase.

messages.label: 201 label B
messages.note: Label B is bought and printed; A is billed and never used.

messages.label: invoice: A and B
messages.note: Weeks later the invoice lists two labels for one shipment.

messages.label: A has no row → void A
messages.note: The reconciler finds A unmatched and files a void or refund. Catching it is good; not causing it is better.

scenarios.name: Request never arrived
scenarios.summary: The lookup says the carrier never saw the purchase, so buying now is safe, with the same reference.

messages.label: POST /labels ref=shp_ab12
messages.note: This time the request itself is dropped before the carrier sees it.

messages.label: GET /labels?ref=shp_ab12
messages.note: Same timeout, same rule: look it up.

messages.label: 404 no such ref
messages.note: Nothing was bought.

messages.label: POST /labels ref=shp_ab12
messages.note: Buy now, with the same reference, so a second lost reply is still recoverable.

scenarios.name: Carrier honours keys
scenarios.summary: If the carrier accepts an Idempotency-Key, a plain retry is safe: the carrier replays the first label instead of buying another.

messages.label: POST /labels Idempotency-Key
messages.note: The shipment reference doubles as the key.

messages.label: 201 label + tracking no.
messages.note: Reply lost as before.

messages.label: POST /labels same key
messages.note: Retry the same call with backoff; no lookup endpoint needed.

messages.label: 201 replayed label
messages.note: The carrier recognises the key and returns the original label. Check how long it keeps keys.
